name: Reza Abiri
title: Assistant Professor
fitReason: Strong applied CS fit for learned shared autonomy, multimodal perception and user-intent modeling on assistive robot arms. Evaluation, intent uncertainty or multimodal robustness are plausible bounded project topics, conditional on mentor approval and the visit timeline.

physicalEvidence.summary: The full May 2025 ARAS preprint describes DQN-based shared autonomy on a real Kinova JACO2 with an overhead RealSense camera and 23 healthy participants. Limited left/right keyboard input drives learned assistance for cup pick-and-place. The nominally autonomous comparison is explicitly a hidden professional operator, not a separate autonomous policy; the ARAS condition itself is learned assistance. This is real robot execution but not clinical efficacy, actual brain-signal control, or unrestricted seven-DoF dexterity. The earlier STREAMS full manuscript also documents five participants using noisy head-motion input with a physical Kinova Jaco. By contrast, January 2026 BRACE uses human cursor control plus Reacher/Fetch simulation, and is counted as current methods activity rather than new physical deployment.

shortVisit.summary: The full lab Open Positions page is explicitly titled PhD Positions and asks interested PhD candidates to email a CV subject to funding. No external-master’s visitor or eight-week summer invitation was established. The university has a separately published international Student Intern route, but institutional eligibility does not establish this lab’s intake.
